title: halfwatch-action-bulletin-naomi-2027-09-13
content:
Half-watch log — 2027-09-13 (Naomi Chen)

Summary:
- Short pager at 02:41 UTC: multiple 5xxs from hosted-api + elevated redis latency. Pager duty: INC-4839.
- Primary impact window: ~02:37–03:05 UTC. Saw spike in tail latencies and transient pod evictions in runtime pool-3.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled runtime pool-3 by +3 replicas, forced graceful restart of sidecar (restart order: sidecar -> app).

Timeline (rough):
- 02:35 UTC — alert fires: redis avg_latency_p50=32ms, p95=410ms, p99=1280ms for instance rdb-prod-07.
- 02:37 — 02:42 UTC — application error rate climbs (5xx ~3% global; concentrated on /v1/generate).
- 02:38 — observed several OOMKilled events on node ip-10-2-17-45; kube evicted 2 runtime pods after OOMs.
- 02:41 — Pager sent. I took lead.
- 02:44 — scaled runtime pool-3 from 6->9 (kubectl scale).
- 02:50 — manually restarted envoy sidecar on affected pods; error rate dropped to ~0.4% by 02:58.
- 03:05 — declared mitigated; kept increased replica count for 15m observation window.

Hypothesis / Root cause (initial):
- Likely combination of a redis slow node (network hiccup) + heavier-than-usual batch request patterns causing KV cache pressure and increasing memory usage in runtime pods leading to OOMs and evictions.
- Secondary: sidecar (envoy) route table got stale under churning pods causing some 5xx responses until restarts.

Commands run (notes, reproducible):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide
- kubectl logs -n prod <pod> -c sidecar --since=10m | grep -i error
- kubectl describe pod <evicted-pod> | sed -n '1,200p'
- redis-cli -h rdb-prod-07 --latency-history 1000 1
- kubectl scale deployment runtime-pool-3 --replicas=9 -n prod

Immediate runbook TODOs (to add/update):
- [ ] Add explicit check: if redis avg p95 > 300ms for >2m, escalate to on-call and trigger read-only fallback route. (owner: Omar, JIRA: SRE-2102)
- [ ] Document step: restart envoy sidecar first before app container for faster route recovery. Add snippet and rationale. (owner: Naomi, SRE-2119)
- [ ] Add memory headroom guidance for runtime pools when KV cache enabled for models with >7B params. (owner: Lena)
- [ ] Add automatic scale-up policy for runtime-pool-* on p50 token throughput > X (sketch metric: token/s per replica). (owner: platform-eng)

Follow-ups (post-shift):
- Collect full redis slowlog and correlate with node-level networking metrics (Net RX/TX) for rdb-prod-07 (Action: Lena).
- Capture flamegraphs for runtime pod CPU/alloc around 02:30–02:50 to confirm if GC spikes coincided with OOMs (Action: Naomi).
- Run controlled injection test: simulate KV cache cold-starts + increased batch size to reproduce memory growth pattern (Action: platform team / test harness ticket).

Customer-visible notes:
- No SLA credit triggered (impact was transient and mitigation within 30m), but flag to CS if any customer reported elevated 5xx's. Slack: ping #cs-ops if we get any complaints (Action: Omar).

Quick fixes applied during incident:
- scaled runtime-pool-3 +3 replicas (kept for 15m observation).
- restarted envoy sidecars for 4 affected pods (worked).
- temporarily reduced default batching window for pool-3 from 25ms->15ms via feature flag (rollback if stability issues).

Metrics to capture for postmortem (candidate list):
- redis p95/p99 per node for 24h, focus 00:00–04:00 UTC window.
- pod restart/eviction timeline + node allocatable memory usage.
- token throughput per replica across pools.
- envoys per-pod connection table size and 5xx counts.

Blame matrix / responsibilities (for tracking only):
- Platform infra: investigate redis node rdb-prod-07 network & disk. (Lena)
- Serving runtime: analyze memory growth pattern and add headroom guidance. (Naomi)
- Observability: add a dedicated query and dashboard for runtime-pool eviction patterns and sidecar error correlation. (Omar)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Did the feature-flag tweak to batching meaningfully reduce memory pressure or just lowered request aggregation? Quick A/B check needed.
- Why did only one redis node show p99 blowups (rdb-prod-07)? Could be network blips or hardware. Check cloud provider maintenance window.
- Consider adding graceful drain sequence to node autoscaler to avoid mid-epoch evictions for runtime pools.

Postmortem checklist (sparse draft):
- [ ] Assemble timeline + logs + traces (owner: Naomi)
- [ ] Add root cause narrative and evidence (owner: Lena)
- [ ] Action items + owners + due dates (owner: Omar)

Notes to self (quick reminders):
- Save stack traces to /tmp/oncall/INC-4839-20270913.tgz before cluster rotates logs.
- Follow up with platform on whether rdb-prod-07 is scheduled for maintenance.
- Add runbook snippet on sidecar restart order (I keep forgetting to update runbook after 2 previous incidents).

Small ergonomics ideas (future):
- Small CLI script on oncall box: rdb-check <node> that returns p50/p95/p99 + last 5mins ops/sec and a quick health verdict. Could have quick 'should-scale' heuristic.
- Feature: platform telemetry signal that flags when envoy conn table > 2000 for >2m per pod.

End notes: felt messy, need cleaner guardrails for cache-cold spikes. Keep this as the working draft for the long-form postmortem.

-- Naomi
